title: Google Business Profile Posts for Black Friday and Christmas
description: How to create offers, updates and events on your Google Business Profile for Black Friday and Christmas: steps, Valencia business examples and a checklist.
h1: Google Business Profile posts for Black Friday and Christmas

answer.question: How do I post a Black Friday offer on my Google listing?
answer.text: Go to your Business Profile from business.google.com, open "Posts", click "Add post" and choose the "Offer" type. According to Google's official help, an offer needs a title and start and end dates and times, and automatically includes the "View offer" button; the description, photo, coupon code, link and terms are optional. You can schedule it with "Schedule this post" so it goes live on the day you choose.

intro: Black Friday and the Christmas campaign are almost here, and your Google listing is the shop window people see when they find you on their phone. Posts let you share an offer, an update or an event right there, without the customer having to visit your website. Here is how to do them well, with examples from local businesses in Valencia.

body.text: Why posts are worth using these weeks

Posts are small free ads that appear on your listing when someone finds you on Google Search or Maps. They do not replace your website or social media, but they have a clear advantage: they are seen at the exact moment a person is deciding whom to call or where to go. In high-demand periods such as Black Friday or Christmas shopping, a customer comparing three hair salons or three toy shops appreciates seeing at a glance that one of them has an active promotion or special hours.

Many Valencia businesses have a verified listing but not a single post. It is an easy gap to fill: it costs no money, takes ten minutes and makes you think about what you want to say. Do not expect miracles, though, and do not promise your team a specific sales increase: a post is support, not a guarantee. What you can control is keeping the information clear, truthful and up to date.
The three post types and when to use each
Google's official help (Business Profile, "Create and manage posts") distinguishes three types. Choosing the right type is half the work.

items: Update: for sharing information about your business, such as news, a new product or a notice. It supports a description, photo, video and an action button with a link. Google says the button must lead to a page where the customer can complete the action, for example booking, ordering online or finding out more.
Offer: for promotions and discounts. It requires a title and start and end dates and times, and adds the "View offer" button. You can include a coupon code, a link and terms and conditions.

Event: to announce a specific date, such as an open day or a tasting. It requires a title and start and end dates and times. If you do not set times, Google explains the event is shown as lasting 24 hours.

body.text: A practical example: a physiotherapy clinic can use an Update to announce its Christmas hours, a clothes shop in Ruzafa can use an Offer for its Black Friday week, and a restaurant in El Carmen can use an Event for its New Year's Eve menu.
Step by step: create your first post

items: Go to business.google.com with the account that manages your listing and open your Business Profile.
Click "Posts" and then "Add post".
Choose the type: Update, Offer or Event.
Upload your own well-lit photo or video. Avoid blurry images or images with too much text.
Write a descriptive title and a short text with the essentials: what you offer, until when and on what terms.
Add the button or coupon code with "Add" if relevant, and check that the link goes to a page that works on mobile.
If you want to get ahead, turn on "Schedule this post" and choose a date and time. You can also set weekly, monthly or custom repeats.
Click "Publish". To edit or delete it later, use the three-dot menu next to the post.

body.text: Keep in mind that Google reviews posts after you submit them. You will see one of these statuses: "Published", visible on Search and Maps; "Pending", not yet visible because it is being processed or because the profile is not verified; or "Not approved", not visible and with a note of the policy that was breached. If your listing is not yet verified, start there with our guide to creating and verifying your Google Business listing.
What to write: ideas for Black Friday and Christmas

The most common mistake is posting something generic like "Great deals!". Specifics work much better, because they answer the customer's question: what, how much and until when. Some ideas by type of business:

items: Hair salon: "Treatment and haircut vouchers, valid until 31 December. Book your appointment before 15 December". Include the link to your booking system.
Restaurant: an Event with the Christmas Eve or New Year's Eve menu, with date, time and booking terms. If you take orders for hampers or takeaway menus, say so in an Update.
Garage: an Offer for a pre-winter check-up with clear dates and the terms in writing, with no hidden small print.
Dental or physiotherapy clinic: an Update with special holiday hours and how to book. If your hours change, also update them in the listing; we cover this in our guide on holiday hours.
Neighbourhood shop: a Black Friday Offer with the product or category in the title, the percentage or price and the exact start and end dates.

body.title: Always clear dates and conditions
body.text: If you announce a discount, state the end date and the main conditions. Avoid promises you cannot keep and do not compare with "previous" prices you never actually applied: besides risking problems with your customers, consumer law requires offers to be truthful. If in doubt, check with your accountant or the official consumer information.
What not to do: Google's policies

Google's official help lists several restrictions worth knowing before you post. According to the page, posts with a phone number in the description may be rejected if it cannot be verified that it belongs to your business; it is better to use the button and the phone number already on your listing. Links must go to trustworthy sites, and Google asks you to avoid spelling mistakes, extra characters, text with no value and automatically generated content. Content must be respectful and family-friendly.

If your business is in a regulated sector, such as alcohol, tobacco, pharmaceuticals, gambling, fireworks or financial services, Google allows posts but without content about those products. If you have a wine shop or a fireworks shop in Valencia, post about your hours or an event, not about the product. Always read the content policy in Google's official help before launching a big campaign.

One note on duration: Google says posts older than six months are archived unless you set a period. So do not leave a forgotten Black Friday offer up; edit or delete it when it ends so nobody turns up at your shop expecting a discount that no longer exists.
A simple calendar for the coming weeks

You do not need to post every day. A light calendar you can keep up without stress is enough, because a well-kept listing with a few useful posts does better than one abandoned after an enthusiastic start.

items: This week: publish your Black Friday offer or news with exact dates, and schedule the end date.
First week of December: publish an Update with your holiday hours and how to book or make an appointment.
Mid-December: publish your gift, voucher or Christmas menu campaign, or an Event if you have a specific date.
Between Christmas and Epiphany (6 January): update hours and announce closures. Remove anything that has expired.
January: ask for reviews from customers who bought during the campaign; we have a guide on how to get Google reviews.

body.text: How to tell whether it is working

Posts are not magic, but you can check whether the effort pays off. Look at how many calls, direction requests and website visits you get before and after, and ask customers how they found you. If you use links with tracking parameters, you will be able to tell in your analytics tool which visits come from your listing. If you do not measure anything yet, start with the basics: Search Console and Analytics, which we explain in another guide.

items: I chose the right type: Update, Offer or Event.
The title is descriptive and says what I offer.
The start and end dates and times are correct.
The photo is my own, sharp and without too much text.
The button or link goes to a page that works on mobile.
I have not put a phone number in the text, and there are no spelling mistakes.
My sector is not regulated, or I am not talking about the restricted product.
I have scheduled or noted the date to remove the offer when it ends.
The holiday hours on the listing match what I am announcing.

faq.q: How many posts can I have on my listing at once?
faq.a: Google's official help does not set a specific number on the page we checked. A sensible approach is to keep a few current, useful posts and remove those that have expired.

faq.q: How long is a post shown?
faq.a: Google says posts older than 6 months are archived unless you set a period. Offers and events also have their own start and end dates.

faq.q: Can I schedule posts in advance?
faq.a: Yes. When creating the post you can turn on "Schedule this post" and choose a date and time, and also set weekly, monthly or custom repeats.

faq.q: Why does my post show as "Pending" or "Not approved"?
faq.a: "Pending" means it is still being processed or the profile is not verified; "Not approved" means it breaches a Google policy, and the listing itself shows which one. Fix the text or image and publish it again.

faq.q: Can I put my phone number in the post text?
faq.a: Google warns that posts with a phone number in the description may be rejected if it cannot be verified that it belongs to your business. It is better to use the action button and the phone number on your listing.

faq.q: Do posts work if my listing is not verified?
faq.a: A post on an unverified profile stays "Pending" and is not visible. Verify your listing first, then post.
